title: feat(QPBT/Combining): preserve supplied polynomial consistency
body:
### Motivation

Issues #362 and #364 include two supplied-witness polynomial consistency
interfaces whose completed proofs were stranded in old PRs #363 and #365.
Main's later projective rounding results do not expose the same three
unrounded scalar bounds. These are auxiliary results used in the first proof
paragraph of paper `lem:qld-4-7`
(`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1267-1289`).

### Description

Preserve the tuple-measurement interface and the ordinary scalar `PolyMeas`
interface on current main. Both retain their original supplied point and line
witness hypotheses, quantifier order, expanded local spaces, and three exact
`deltaLd` conclusions. The passing premise is derived internally; the named
`directPassingErrorEnvelope` is definitionally equal to the original expression.

The scalar proof reuses the tuple interface, coordinate marginalization,
consistency data processing, and PR #623's public supplied-point identity.
Two separate auxiliary blueprint entries state the hypotheses explicitly.
The mathematical name replaces the old scalar theorem's `Native` wording.
Original proof and review provenance is retained in the issue-364 brief.

Neither result asserts projectivity, polynomial separation, or the full
source paired-polynomial conclusion. The qualifications tracked in #527,
#598, and #524 are unchanged. Original PRs remain preserved pending this
packet's review and integration.

### Testing

- Focused Lean checks and module builds passed for both new modules.
- Both public theorems' axiom closures contain only `propext`,
  `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound`.
- Normal commit hooks and whitespace checks passed; the worktree is clean.
- The author did not run full CI or blueprint rendering. Its initial
  `checkdecls` attempt could not run because the generated declaration list
  was absent; the normal publication and CI path must regenerate and verify it.

---
Addresses #364
Addresses #362

title: docs(qpbt): state the operator bound in Closeness docstrings
body:
### Motivation

Review 5250819632 of PR #212 identified five Closeness docstrings whose use of "square-summable" obscured the actual operator relation. This packet preserves that documentation correction on current main for #117.

### Description

State the sum-of-adjoint-products relation in the module docstring and four theorem docstrings in `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Points/Closeness.lean`. Preserve the uniform-distribution assumption and current field-valued gap-note citation. The diff is 14 insertions and 11 deletions, all in comments; no statement, proof, import or attribute changes.

This addresses #212 review finding F3 only. F2's blueprint traceability remains separate work, and #212 stays open until that disposition is complete. Formalization auxiliaries may cite the paper argument they support without being presented as separately named paper statements.

### Testing

- Exact head `3ca3747a19de9c396f4eda193ef805778c507531`: all nine canonical CI contexts succeeded; summary reports 885 seconds. Blueprint rendering was skipped because no blueprint source changed.
- The helper's supplemental blueprint axiom audit reports 1,749 passed, zero failed.
- Focused Lean checking and ordinary pre-push checks passed. No proof holes or bypasses are introduced.

---
Addresses #117

title: feat(local): soft-landing pause and work-resuming resume (issue #560)
body:
### Motivation

Closes #560. Every pause so far has been a hard landing: the 2026-09-12 chain killed
17 codex sessions mid-work, and the 2026-09-14 fallout was reviewers that "exited 143",
kill-caused `daemon/pr<N>.failed` markers that made the merge daemon skip PRs for two
hours, and lanes restarted from scratch on heads that already carried a green CI and a
finished review. A codex session has already paid for its input and its reasoning, so a
kill throws that away and the resume pays again.

Stacked on `issue-550-full-speed-v2` (PR #552), like #554 and #556.

### Description

**Two owner words.** `owner-pause.sh --cutoff` stops admission and nothing else — caps to
0 through run-mode, `watchdog/drain`, no signal, no daemon stopped — and may be given long
before the pause. `owner-pause.sh` (no flag) is the pause word and starts the deadline from
`run.pause_deadline_min`. A pause without a prior cutoff degrades to the landing rule.

**Age-based landing.** At the pause word `local/bin/pause_landing.py` classifies every live
codex session from the spool and `/proc`: young sessions (under `young_max_min`) stop at
once, a mature reviewer runs to the last call and is then restarted from scratch, and a
mature writer is checkpointed — worktree untouched, thread id, worktree, step and elapsed
time recorded — and stopped only at the last call. Every threshold lives in
`local/capacity-policy.json`; no number is written into a shell script.

**Pause manifest.** `watchdog/pause-state.json` gains a `landing` key: the resolved
thresholds, each lane with its issue, branch, head, the step it reached, its head's
statuses and its own environment, each stopped session with thread id, role, worktree,
elapsed time and resumability, and the `daemon/pr<N>.failed` markers the pause caused,
recorded by difference against a snapshot taken at T+0:00.

**Resuming the work.** `owner-resume.sh` replays that manifest after its post-condition
check: each parked lane at the step it reached (no merge/build/push on an unchanged head,
no CI when `local-ci/summary` is already success, no review when `local-review/summary` is,
nothing at all when both are), each checkpointed writer the lane does not own on its own
codex thread through `dispatch.sh --resume`, each stopped reviewer from scratch, and each
recorded marker cleared.

**Prover milestone rule.** The prover dispatch prompt and `local/personas/prover.md` carry
"commit each proved lemma in the worktree, with the hooks running, before starting the
next one", and the continue prompt tells a resumed prover to read its worktree and continue
from that state. A kill then costs at most the work since the last commit.

### Review findings and how each was addressed

Two independent reviews produced 33 findings (9 blockers, 13 major, 7 minor, 4 nits; several
were reported by both reviews). All are addressed; none is disputed.

**Blockers**

| Finding | Addressed |
|---|---|
| `resume_plan` emits a parked lane AND the session that lane owns: two writers in one worktree, a merge and a build in a tree codex is editing, a branch claim the loser dies 5 on | `lane_owned()`: a lane owns every session in its worktree or on its branch. Only the lane is relaunched, and `lane.sh` resumes the thread from `<state>/<issue>.thread`; the session is listed as owned, with argv `None`. Test: `test_a_lane_and_its_own_worker_are_never_both_launched`, whose fixture puts lane 7 and `prover-7-a` on one worktree |
| `lane_resume_step` falls through to `publish`, so a lane killed mid-work publishes a half-finished worktree through PR, CI and review | `publish` only for a lane that reached publication (recorded step `publish`/`ci`/`review`); `warm` and `dispatch` resume at `dispatch`, which reuses the lane's thread record. Tests: `test_a_lane_stopped_before_publication_resumes_at_dispatch`, `test_a_lane_that_reached_publication_resumes_at_publish` |
| The resume is not idempotent: a second `owner-resume.sh` relaunches every lane and every session again | `resume-exec` stamps `landing.replayed_at` plus one `replay` row per item; `resume-plan`/`resume-exec` then emit nothing without `--force`. Test: `test_a_replayed_manifest_launches_nothing_a_second_time` |
| The post-condition requires `watchdog/paused`, which nothing ever creates, so the whole work-resume block was unreachable after a real pause | `stop_admission` writes `$W/paused` next to `$W/drain`. Tests: `test_the_pause_writes_every_marker_the_resume_requires` (every marker the post-condition requires must be one the pause writes) and an end-to-end `owner-pause.sh --cutoff` against a scratch cache root |
| The landing signals the `dispatch.sh` wrapper, not codex: its TERM trap is deferred while the `codex \| tee` pipeline is in the foreground, so codex keeps spending quota and the SIGKILL skips `cleanup()` | `terminate()` signals the recorded pid **and** its process tree (`Processes.ppid` + `descendants`), which ends codex and lets the wrapper's own TERM trap and `cleanup` run; after a SIGKILL, `free_locks()` releases the account slot, the branch claim and the spool row explicitly. Tests: `test_the_codex_child_is_signalled_with_its_dispatcher`, `test_a_killed_wrapper_has_its_slot_claim_and_spool_row_freed`, `test_a_session_that_stops_on_term_keeps_its_locks` |
| The grace is slept once per session, so a phase costs `grace_s x sessions` and runs past the deadline | `land()` is two passes: one SIGTERM pass, ONE sleep, then SIGKILL to the survivors. Test: `test_the_grace_is_slept_once_for_the_phase_not_once_per_session` (17 sessions, `slept == [grace_s]`) |
| The resume dispatch drops the job class, effort, hardness reason, persona, sandbox and account, so `account_router` refuses the resume with "resume cannot switch model" and nothing is relaunched | `RESUME_FIELD_FLAGS` carries `--job-class`, `--effort`, `--hardness-reason`, `--account`, the recorded `--sandbox`, and `--persona`/`--persona-ref` when the recorded label has the `<ref>:<path>` shape it was built from. Tests: `test_a_checkpointed_prover_is_resumed_on_its_own_thread`, `test_the_sandbox_is_the_one_the_session_was_dispatched_with` |

**Major**

| Finding | Addressed |
|---|---|
| The recycled-pid guard is not fail-closed: an unreadable cmdline is signalled unverified, and any `dispatch.sh` cmdline satisfies it for any record | `is_ours()`: an empty command line is `not-ours`, `dispatch.sh` is necessary and never sufficient, and the recorded name, worktree or `--role <r> --issue <i>` pair must appear. Tests: `test_an_unreadable_command_line_is_spared_not_signalled`, `test_a_different_dispatch_on_a_recycled_pid_is_not_ours`, `test_the_recorded_worktree_identifies_a_real_dispatcher` |
| `failed_markers` is always empty: the snapshot is taken ten minutes after the only process that writes such a marker was stopped | New `markers` subcommand, called at T+0:00 before the daemon-stop phase; `manifest` keeps an existing snapshot. Tests: `test_the_marker_snapshot_is_taken_before_the_daemon_is_stopped`, `test_a_second_manifest_keeps_the_first_landings_record` |
| The lane relaunch drops `LANE_BRANCH`, `SKIP_REVIEW`, `MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_CMD` | `live_lanes` reads `/proc/<pid>/environ` and records them; `LANE_BRANCH` also decides the recorded branch and worktree, and `lane_env()` re-emits them. Test: `test_a_lanes_own_environment_is_recorded_with_it` |
| A checkpointed writer whose thread id was not captured is stopped and then silently never put back | It gets a fresh `dispatch.sh` with `RESTART_PROMPT` (read the worktree, continue from that state); a session that genuinely cannot be rebuilt is printed as `STOPPED AND NOT PUT BACK`. Tests: `test_a_writer_without_a_thread_id_gets_a_fresh_session_not_silence`, `test_a_session_that_cannot_be_rebuilt_is_named_loudly` |
| A failed landing phase is invisible because the pipeline's status comes from `sed`, and the last call is not a superset | `land_phase()` checks `PIPESTATUS[0]`; `land --phase last` stops everything still `pending`, whatever its recorded action. Tests: `test_a_failed_landing_phase_is_not_swallowed_by_the_pipe`, `test_the_last_call_also_stops_a_row_an_earlier_phase_missed` |
| After a `--cutoff`, the pause word records the already-zeroed caps | The caps come from `saved_caps` (then `derived.caps`); the live-file readers are skipped while a cutoff is in force; `write_state` refuses to lower an already-recorded nonzero cap to zero. Test: `test_a_recorded_cap_is_never_lowered_to_zero_by_a_later_write` |
| Lanes relaunched as `env LANE_RESUME_STEP=… lane.sh …` match neither `LANE_RE` nor the sweep, so they are invisible to every later pause | The relaunch is `["bash", lane.sh, issue, slug, role]` with the step in the Popen environment. Test: `test_the_relaunch_argv_is_one_the_next_pause_can_still_see`, which checks the argv against both `LANE_RE` and the sweep's own patterns |

**Minor**

| Finding | Addressed |
|---|---|
| A head carrying a finished review re-runs the review | `lane_env()` adds `SKIP_REVIEW=1` when `local-review/summary` is success on the unchanged head. Test: `test_a_pending_ci_resumes_at_ci_and_skips_the_finished_review` |
| Running the pause twice destroys the first landing's record | `merge_manifest()` keeps every row the first landing stopped and the earliest `markers_before` |
| One failed launch aborts the rest of the resume plan | Each launch is guarded; the row records `FAILED to launch: …`, the plan continues, and the command exits 4 with a summary. `owner-resume.sh` treats 4 as a partial replay, not a total failure. Test: `test_one_failed_launch_does_not_cost_the_rest_of_the_plan` |
| The `last_call_s` shell fallback is 60 while the policy and the module say 90 | Changed to 90, and `test_every_shell_fallback_equals_the_modules_default` now asserts every `pl_get KEY fallback` literal against `pause_landing.DEFAULTS` |
| `watchdog/cutoff` is never cleared, so every cutoff after the first is silent | `owner-resume.sh` removes it, and a marker older than `cutoff_lead_min` is re-asserted with a fresh message. Test: `test_the_resume_clears_the_cutoff_marker` |

**Nits**

| Finding | Addressed |
|---|---|
| `--sandbox workspace-write` hardcoded on every thread-resume | `str(session.get("sandbox") or "workspace-write")` |
| `manifest` can spend up to `STATUS_BUDGET_S` on GitHub before a single session is stopped | The landing runs `manifest --no-github`, then `land --phase now`, then the new `statuses` subcommand. Test: `test_the_statuses_are_read_after_the_young_are_stopped` |
| The lane scan matches every pid on the host, so another user's `lane.sh` is recorded and relaunched | Scoped, but **by owner uid, not by script path**: the live fleet starts lanes as `setsid nohup bash /tmp/lane-v17.sh N slug prover`, so requiring `checkout/local/bin` would have made every real lane invisible to the pause — a worse failure than the one being fixed. `Processes.owner_uid` drops any pid this user does not own. Test: `test_another_users_lane_is_not_this_runs_work` |
| The landing thresholds still appear as `pl_get` fallback literals, and the guard test cannot catch a wrong one | The header now states plainly that the fallbacks are deliberate and are pinned by a test, and the test compares each one to `pause_landing.DEFAULTS` |

### Testing

`python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_*.py'` — **1141 tests, OK (skipped=9)**,
which is the runner `local/bin/ci.sh` and `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml` use (`pytest` is not
installed for this user on the host). `test_pause_landing.py` alone: 72 tests, OK.

Dry runs against a scratch `MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT`, touching no live state:

* `pause_landing.py thresholds` reads `local/capacity-policy.json`: `young_max_min 5`,
  `cutoff_lead_min 10`, `landing_lead_s 180`, `last_call_s 90`, `grace_s 20`;
* `owner-pause.sh --dry-run` prints the seven phases (landing T+12:00, last call T+13:30,
  confirm/record T+14:00 for a 15-minute deadline) plus the landing rule and the source of
  every threshold;
* `owner-pause.sh --cutoff --dry-run` prints the cutoff plan and signals nothing.

### Per-commit line counts (scaffolding budget 1000)

| Commit | Changed lines |
|---|---|
| `fix(local): stop the codex behind the wrapper, and replay a manifest once` | 603 (527+, 76−) — `local/bin/pause_landing.py` |
| `fix(telemetry): write the paused marker, keep the real caps, fail the phase` | 224 (177+, 47−) — `owner-pause.sh`, `owner-resume.sh`, owner-tools `README.md` |
| `test(scripts): the two-pass landing, lane ownership and the replay stamp` | 527 (490+, 37−) — `scripts/tests/test_pause_landing.py`, `local/protocols/full-speed-mode.md` |

No commit uses `MIPSTARRE_INFRA_OVERRIDE`; every hook ran.

title: feat(local): hot-editable accounts file, the owner CLI and the GitHub control channel
body:
### Motivation

The owner's capacity is not a fact of the run; it changes during it. One to three endpoints,
each with one or two API keys, each key's concurrency limit somewhere between 5 and 40 and
moving while work is going on: the endpoint's admin reassigns slots, the owner wins them
back, a key becomes invalid, a key runs out of quota. On 2026-09-12 every one of those
events reached the pipeline as a message to a session that had to be idle to receive it, and
the caps were then edited by hand ten times.

W1 (#550, this PR's base) fixed the *start* of a run: one brief, one mode file, one accessor.
It did not fix the *middle*. The brief is one-shot by design, so changing a ceiling meant
re-applying it and re-seeding every derived value, and nothing at all let the owner add or
retire a key. Worse, two key names were hard-coded through the layer —
`account_router.ACCOUNTS = ("primary", "second")`, `run_mode.ACCOUNT_NAMES`, `dispatch.sh`'s
`for account in primary second`, the `--account` choices, the second key's `CODEX_HOME` as an
`if` rather than a field — so a third key could not be expressed at all.

This PR makes the set of usable keys and their ceilings a **live, owner-owned file** that the
running pipeline re-reads, editable from a shell or from GitHub, with no prompt to any
session and no re-brief.

### Description

**1. One live file.** `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/watchdog/accounts.json` is the source of truth
for admission: one entry per key, `{name, label, endpoint, codex_home, ceiling,
external_reserved, enabled, note}`, any number of endpoints and keys. **No key value is ever
stored in it** — an entry names the codex home the key lives in, which only the owner
touches. `local/bin/accounts_file.py` owns the schema, the validation, the atomic write
(temp file + `os.replace`, validation strictly before it, so a reader a millisecond later
never sees a half-file), the `watchdog/capacity/accounts.log` audit line and the `ACCOUNTS:`
directive grammar — so the CLI and the GitHub channel cannot disagree about what a valid
entry is. `run_mode.py apply` **seeds** the file from the brief when it is absent and never
overwrites an existing one; where it exists, it is what `apply` reads, so re-applying a brief
to change the speed tier cannot undo an hour of ceiling edits.

**2. Re-read every tick, with ceiling semantics.** The capacity controller loads it on every
tick and `account_router.py` on every reservation (at most 60 s stale). `ceiling` is a
ceiling and never a target: the AIMD discovery is unchanged below it and may never exceed
`ceiling - external_reserved`. Lowering it takes effect at the next tick; raising it lets the
additive creep continue rather than jumping the cap. `enabled: false` and a removed entry are
cap 0 with no probe — and the router reads the flag directly, which closes the up-to-60-second
window between the owner's edit and the controller's tick. An **invalid** file is a hard,
named failure with the cap files untouched; falling back to the brief would restore the
ceiling the owner has just lowered.

**3. Measured health, with a reason.** `auth` (401/403, invalid key) and
`insufficient_balance` (`INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`, quota) are marked `"disables": true` in
`local/capacity-policy.json` and take the key to cap 0 at the **first** occurrence — a `401`
is not a statistic, and no amount of AIMD makes an invalid key valid. `endpoint_5xx` keeps
its 3-in-120 s threshold. Both record `reason` and `disabled_by`, in the per-account health
files and in the new `watchdog/capacity/health.json` (one document for every key). The way
back is the same half-open, single-flight, read-only probe restoring cap **1**, with the
key-invalid backoff starting at five minutes rather than thirty seconds.
`capacity_controller.py probe [ACCOUNT]` runs it on demand.

**4. Two owner touchpoints, neither of them a prompt.**
`results/telemetry/owner-tools/accounts.sh list|get|set|enable|disable|add|remove|probe|log`
is the shell one, installed by the versioned installer. For when there is no shell, a comment
on the owner inbox issue in the form `ACCOUNTS: <name> ceiling=<n> [reserved=<n>]
[enabled=true|false]` is applied by a sixth janitor pass (`local/bin/accounts_inbox.py`) and
answered with one reply per comment saying exactly what took effect. Only the repository
owner login recorded in `local/README.md` is applied; anyone else's comment is answered with
a `rejected:` line naming them, so an attempt is visible rather than silent. A comment is
applied **exactly once** (the reply carries its comment id), so a sweep every minute cannot
re-apply a ceiling the owner has since changed at the shell. The channel carries `ceiling`,
`reserved`, `enabled` and `note` only: an endpoint or a codex home is a path on the host and
is set at the shell, where a typo cannot travel through a public comment. Comment bodies stay
untrusted text — only `ACCOUNTS:` lines are read, every value is validated before anything is
written, and nothi

---
Closes #555

title: feat(local): chsh build farm for full speed mode, with an automatic local fallback
body:
### Motivation

The 2026-09-12 full speed run was compute-bound, not idea-bound: ghz carries 128 cores
shared with other users, the run sat at load 90-150 for four hours, the median CI build was
61 s and every lane queued behind the machine-wide full-build lease. A second machine was
prepared that day and has been idle since — `chsh`, 192 aarch64 cores, 2 TB RAM, 10 TB
free, Lean 4.32.0, a byte-identical copy of the Mathlib package cache, a hardlink build
seed and a checkout mirroring this one, reachable from ghz at 86.7 MB/s. Measured there: a
cold lane offload 14.9 s, a one-file rebuild 17.2 s round trip, a full warm build 19 min.

Nothing was wired: the offload existed only as a draft script outside the repository, the
mode layer had no field saying whether a run may use a second host, and a lane that tried
would have failed whenever chsh was unreachable.

The owner's rule is narrow and this PR implements exactly it: **in full speed mode the
compute and the storage of chsh are used alongside ghz; outside full speed mode chsh is
never used**, and **no codex session ever runs on chsh** (its own internet is ~16 KB/s; it
is a pure build node fed from ghz by rsync).

### Description

**1. The gate is the run mode, and nothing else.** `run.compute.offload_hosts` in the run
brief, validated at briefing time against the known hosts (an unknown name is an exit 2
naming the key, not a host nobody has keys for). `run_mode.py get offload` answers `yes`
only when `run.speed` is `fast`, the host is listed and the run is not paused; a
default-speed run, a brief without the field, a paused run, an unreadable mode and a
run-mode document written before the field all answer `no`. `get offload_reason` prints
the sentence that decided it, `get offload_hosts` the list, and `show` carries a line. A
pause turns the farm off with everything else, `set speed` moves it with the tier, and
there is no environment variable that turns it *on* — `MIPSTARRE_OFFLOAD=0` can only turn
it further off.

**2. `results/telemetry/owner-tools/build-on-chsh.sh`**, the side session's draft hardened
into a tracked tool: `BatchMode` ssh over the internal address (`HostName 192.168.1.18`,
port 22) with `StrictHostKeyChecking=yes` against a known-hosts file the installer
deploys at `watchdog/chsh/known_hosts`; one `flock` per lane; a toolchain equality check;
lane names and lake targets validated before they reach a remote shell; the six steps of
the design (push sources excluding `.lake`, `.git`, `.worktrees` and `results/telemetry`;
`cp -al` from the shared seed; the shared Mathlib symlink; `lake build`; return only what
the build wrote under `.lake/build/{lib,ir}`; exit with lake's code); a `--dry-run` that
prints every command and contacts chsh not at all; a `--check` that reports the gate; and
one row per build in `watchdog/chsh/offload.log` naming the host. Without `--dry-run` the
script refuses to contact chsh at all unless the run mode says `yes`, so the owner's rule
is enforced in the tool and not only in its callers.

**3. The fallback is the point.** `local/bin/offload-build.sh` is the single copy of the
rule that `lane.sh` (pre-push build and changed-module build) and `ci.sh` (the
`local-ci/build` step) share. Exit 64 (chsh unusable — unreachable, missing host keys,
busy lane, toolchain mismatch) and 65 (artifacts not returned) fall back to the local
build, which then decides the step; **every other exit code is the build's own verdict and
is passed through**, because a proof that does not compile on chsh does not compile here
either and a silent local retry would spend the single full-build lease twice to learn the
same thing. A lane can never fail because chsh is unreachable, and the log always names
the host that built.

**4. The seed.** A merge moves `main` and leaves chsh's checkout and hardlink seed behind,
so the next offloaded lane rebuilds the difference — slow, never wrong. The merge daemon
fires `build-on-chsh.sh --seed-refresh` after every merge: detached, under its own lock, at
most once an hour, and an immediate no-op while the offload is disabled.

**5. Installation.** `install.sh` deploys the script under the same hash manifest as every
other operator tool (optional entry: a checkout without it installs as before) and copies
the farm's host keys to `watchdog/chsh/known_hosts` from `$MIPSTARRE_CHSH_KNOWN_HOSTS`
(default `/tmp/chsh-setup/known_hosts`). The keys are runtime state and are not committed;
a missing file makes the offload unusable — which costs build time and nothing else — and
is never a reason to accept an unknown host key. Nothing is installed on chsh.

**6. Runbook.** `local/protocols/full-speed-mode.md` §5.1: what chsh is, the rule, the

title: feat(local): owner run brief, run-mode and standing reports for full speed mode
body:
### Motivation

The full speed run of 2026-09-12 (04:17Z–08:33Z) produced 9 merges and cost the owner
eight distinct classes of manual intervention, each of which is a defect of the workflow
rather than of the mathematics: the concurrency limits restated five times while ~90
worker sessions died (69 on an endpoint that had been answering 503 for an hour, the rest
above an unmeasured provider ceiling); repeated questions about idle slots while every
dispatched fixer was dying at a model-policy preflight; the estimate format dictated by
hand after multi-line prose appeared on the estimate issue; ready PRs sitting open behind
two-hour timer backoffs; three lane-runner revisions hand-patched in `/tmp`; the speed
tier switched three times by string surgery on a generated file; and a terminal stop order
undone five minutes later by a goal keeper that had no way to know about it.

This PR is the whole of the tracker's seven work items: the owner gives **one** briefing at
the start of a run and afterwards receives only the half-hourly one-line estimate and prose
progress on the progress log. Everything else becomes an automatic mechanism, a one-file
switch or a self-healing loop, and every fix that lived in `/tmp` or in one host's
`.git/config` now lives in the repository. The design document is the first comment on
#550.

### Description

**1. Owner briefing, run mode and standing reports.** `local/bin/run_mode.py` validates one
`run-brief.json` and is the single writer of `watchdog/run-mode.json` and of the derived cap
files, and the single accessor for every capacity, schedule, speed and issue number, so no
protocol, persona or script carries a literal that can go stale. `ready_report.py` answers
"ready but open, and why" hourly from daemon state, with `unexplained` as the alarm case.
`estimate_post.py` renders the two prescribed lines and refuses any other body.
`local/protocols/full-speed-mode.md` is the runbook and `local/personas/main.md` gains the
Standing reports duty.

**2. Dispatch and telemetry.** Provider failures are classified (`concurrency_limit`,
`endpoint_5xx`, `retries_exhausted`, `timeout`, `task_failure`, `unknown`) and recorded with
the endpoint, so a capacity refusal is no longer scored like a failed proof; `dispatch.sh`
spools its request and prompt and retries a transient class instead of dying; a branch claim
refuses a second writer with exit 5; the owner model override moves from a PATH-shim rewrite
(which made the registry record a model that never ran) into the policy layer; `autofix.sh`
stops defaulting to a model its own preflight rejects and gains the fix → CI → review loop.

**3. Capacity controller.** An AIMD controller with per-endpoint health is the only writer of
the caps: it measures the real limit under the briefed ceiling, trips to cap 0 on a 5xx
endpoint, recovers through one half-open read-only probe, subtracts declared external
consumers, and carries the measurement into the next run.

**4. Operator tools.** One versioned installer with a hash manifest that refuses to overwrite
a hand patch; one `owner-pause.sh` whose every phase is clamped to the briefed deadline and
which releases queued dispatches rather than killing them; one `owner-resume.sh` that
restores from the recorded state only; one `owner-say.sh` whose terminal mode holds the goal
before it speaks.

**5. Merge daemon and lane runner, promoted.** Honest names in the repository, failure markers
that carry a class and clear on an observable change instead of a timer, PAR sized from the
machine, the lane's build under the machine-wide lease, a retirement pass — and the lane's
`MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS=1` fallback push deleted.

**6. Self-repair janitor.** One idempotent sweep of five passes, each selecting by record
field: no date glob and no filename digit filter anywhere.

**7. Merge hygiene and build reachability.** A committed `.gitattributes` union driver for the
append-only logs, asserted by `worktree-setup.sh`; and a reachability guard inside the
existing `local-ci/build` step that names a module left outside the umbrella import closure.

**No proof-integrity mechanism is touched.** No change to `.githooks/*`,
`merge_loss_guard.py`, `checked-push.sh`, the seven `pr_merge.py` gates, the eight canonical
`local-ci/<step>` contexts or the review-verdict contract. The one place a current tool
*bypassed* a gate — the lane's hook-skipping fallback push — is removed, which strengthens it.

### Testing

Run in the branch worktree on the build host.

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_*.py'` → **977 tests, OK**
  (9 skipped: the historical useful-queue scenarios retired by #505). That is the command the
  pre-commit hook runs, and it ran on every commit here that stages a `scripts/` file.
- `bash -n` on all 24 changed shell files and both renderings of the generated PATH shim: clean.
- `python3 -m py_compile` on all 26 changed Python files: clean. `json.load` on
  `model-policy.json`, `capacity-pol

---
Closes #550

## Description

Reuse of an existing square-summability bound, plus the small clean-ups
that reuse makes possible. After review round three the PR was reduced to
exactly this: every Lean declaration it previously added is already on
main in `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/PointComparison.lean`, so those
modules and the blueprint nodes that tagged them were dropped rather than
duplicated.

What this PR changes against main (four files):

  `sum_norm_sub_apply_sq_le_four`, moved here from
  `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Observables/LineMeasurement/SquareRootError.lean` under

  `def:povm-distance`; no blueprint node claims it.

  declaration is removed from here; its existing call site keeps working
  through the import closure.

  fix on `sum_norm_sum_smul_sq_of_orthogonal` ("`i` ranging over a finite

round addresses F1-F7; F1-F4 and F5 by deleting the duplicate Lean

### Motivation

Stage 4.3 packet for issue #428. The branch opened by restoring the
restricted-average mass split in `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/RestrictedAverage.lean`.
Those three lemmas (`avgOver_restrict_mul_mass`,
`avgOver_restrict_le_div_mass`, `avgOver_le_restrict_add_discarded_mass`) have
since landed on `main` through other PRs, so relative to `main` this branch no
longer contributes any Lean statement or proof. What it still contributes, and
what this PR should be read as, is the blueprint record for the combined point
and line construction plus one Lean module docstring.

### Description

Relative to the merge base with `main` the diff is 401 added and 6 removed
lines in four files, none of them a Lean statement, definition or proof:

- `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex` (+125): a supported-completion
  subsection with `def:supported-completion`,
  `lem:supported-completion-structure`, `lem:supported-completion-relabeling`
  and `lem:supported-completion-restriction`, between them naming all 17 public
  declarations of `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/SupportedCompletion.lean`.
- `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex` (+241):
  `lem:combined-points-unrestricted-error`, `lem:linear-quadratic-agreement`,
  `lem:restricted-average-mass-split` (the conditioning and restoration
  identities of `RestrictedAverage.lean`), `lem:direct-coefficient-resampling`
  and `lem:direct-passing-value`.
- `blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex` (+25):
  `lem:controlled-unitary-membership`.
- `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ExtendedLineGame/DiagonalParameterDefectTransport.lean`
  (+10/-6): module docstring only.

Review round 5254746096 (CHANGES_REQUESTED at `ea00e4c0`) is addressed by the
follow-up commit on this branch:

- F1 `lem:restricted-average-mass-split` no longer claims a probability
  distribution; the statement now matches the linked declarations, which take
  an arbitrary finitely supported nonnegative weighting and normalize only the
  restriction.
- F2 the proof-level `\uses` of `lem:direct-coefficient-resampling` now names
  `lem:sandwich-codeword-defect` and `lem:coefficient-polynomial-agreement`,
  and the prose names the Lean resampling identities that carry the step and
  have no blueprint node.
- F3 the proof-level `\uses` of `lem:direct-passing-value` likewise, and the
  prose now names the per-branch bounds, the collision-loss inequality
  `extendedDirectLd_coefficientCollisionLoss_le_five_mul`, the rejection cap
  `directLdRejectionProbability_le_one` and the capped scalar envelope step.
- F4 the `DiagonalParameterDefectTransport` module docstring now leads with the
  identity being proved instead of with formalization mechanics.
- F5 this title and body.

Base note: the former parent `issue-419-finite-conditional-average` was
merged through PR 424. The PR now targets `main`; the reviewed head is unchanged.

### Testing

- `local/bin/ci.sh 433` (9 gating checks).

  `scripts/audit_unfaithful_markers.py --ci`.

- `lake env lean` on the one touched Lean file.
- No `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom` or `native_decide` is introduced.

Addresses #428
